analysis.title: Preparing a specimon slide for observation
analysis.description: A 4-step horizontal process sequence illustrating how to prepare an onion cell specimen slide for microscopic observation, detailing extraction, mounting, staining, and covering.
analysis.layout: The title is positioned at the top center. Below it, four circular illustrated step containers connected by horizontal directional arrows span from left to right. Beneath each circle is a step header, an explanatory text description, and supplementary cue notes under steps 1 and 4.

components.visibleText: Preparing a specimon slide for observation

Step 1: Extract
Use forceps to peel a thin, transparent layer of tissue (e.g., onion epidermis).
Cue: Must be thin to let light pass through.

Step 2: Mount
Place the specimen flat in the centre of a clean glass slide.

Step 3: Stain
Add a single drop of biological stain over the specimen.

Step 4: Cover
Use a mounted needle to lower a glass coverslip at an angle.
Cue: Lowering at an angle prevents trapping air bubbles under the glass.
